text:
Vasily Podkolzin has become a different player in Edmonton this season. He is playing 17:42 a night, up from 15:23, and is on the ice for 44% of the Oilers' power-play time after 12% last season. With that, 21 points in 25 games (13 goals), and 18th in the league in wins added by goals. He brings the physical side too: 76 hits.

Part of the jump is real. His own chances are up to 1.19 expected goals per 60 (expected goals measure the quality of chances) from 0.78, and Edmonton takes 59% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, far better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries last season.

Part of it is not. He has 13 goals on 8.8 expected, shooting 25% against 14% last season, and the Oilers have scored 12.4 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That finishing rate rarely lasts. What we'd watch is the role, and whether the minutes and power-play time stay.
